title: Can AI apply client feedback to my Premiere Pro edit?
summary: Turn clear client notes into a revised Premiere sequence with an AI assistant, while keeping creative decisions with the editor and the original cut intact.
body_markdown:
## What you’ll take away


- Use the sequence revision the client actually watched.
- Translate subjective feedback into an editorial decision before requesting a change.
- Keep a note-to-change summary with the new cut.


## Which notes are ready for an assistant?


“Remove the sentence about next year’s launch at 00:42” is actionable. “This feels slow” is a creative observation. Both are valuable, but they require different work. The first identifies an operation; the second asks the editor to decide whether the problem is repetition, weak stakes, a long pause, or a picture that holds too long.


You do not need a formal specification for every note. You need enough context to identify the moment and intended change. When the client supplies a broad reaction, propose the choice in plain language: “I’ll remove the repeated explanation and preserve the pause before the result.” That decision becomes a concrete assistant task.


## Start from the version the client reviewed


Timecoded feedback belongs to a particular cut. If the client watched version three and you are already editing version four, the same number may point to another shot. Give Wideframe the existing project, correct sequence, and notes together. Identify the intended new version so its relationship to the reviewed one is clear.


A review export helps explain what the client saw. A note about a title may concern wording, duration, placement, or something visible in that particular render. Resolve the meaning before turning it into an operation. This avoids completing the wrong revision neatly.


## An example revision pass


Consider an illustrative two-minute product overview. The client wants a repeated introduction removed, a pause shortened before the demo, an outdated line replaced, and the ending made “more confident.” The first three become specific changes once the intended source material is identified. The last needs a choice: use a stronger existing closing sentence, remove a hesitant phrase without changing meaning, or request a pickup.


Keep a replacement line in context. Joining fragments should not manufacture a promise the speaker never meant. If no suitable line exists, a pickup request is more useful than an inaccurate polished ending. The intended output is a new sequence with the approved changes and a clear explanation of the unresolved decision.


## Use Wideframe’s review-notes workflow


The[apply-review-notes skill recipe](https://try.wideframe.com/skills/apply-review-notes/) describes matching timecoded notes to clips, creating another sequence version, applying objective operations, and flagging ambiguous feedback. Follow the page’s instructions to add and save the workflow in Wideframe before using its saved name.


Ask for a summary connecting each client note to its change. Back in Premiere, that tells you where to look, what remains your decision, and what to tell the producer. The assistant is useful because it carries out explicit work on the existing edit; a second first-cut generator would not address this particular bottleneck.


## Finish the editorial pass in Premiere


Play across each changed passage, including the lead-in and transition afterward. A removed sentence can leave an unexplained pronoun. A tighter pause can cut off a breath. A replacement shot can make the following image repetitive. These relationships are why the editor still watches the revision as a piece.


Revisit captions and on-screen claims when dialogue changes. Removing a spoken assertion while leaving it in a lower third defeats the note. Listen to music and room tone around new joins, and decide whether the ending lands with the intended emphasis. Correct individual operations do not automatically produce the right overall rhythm.


## Make the next review easier


Send the revised cut with a concise explanation: “The repeated introduction is gone; the demo begins sooner; the replacement uses the approved line; the closing pickup is outstanding.” That gives the client useful decisions instead of implying everything is resolved.


On the next project, reuse the saved workflow with the new sequence and notes. Existing-project work recurs through second cuts, late updates, and new versions of an approved piece. Our[Premiere versioning guide](https://try.wideframe.com/blog/premiere-pro-project-versioning-ai-iterations/) covers file organization, while[tools that work alongside Premiere](https://try.wideframe.com/blog/ai-tools-that-work-with-premiere-pro-not-replace-it/) explains the broader assistant approach.

TRY AN EXAMPLE REQUEST
